abs GET /abs/api/collections#user.why: The seed stage creates two collections moments apart, stored at one-second resolution, and ListUserCollections orders by created_at DESC with no tiebreak. A server whose two writes straddle a second lists the newer first; one whose writes share a second lists them in table order, so the two lists swap. Seen Go vs Go: the same two writes straddling a second on one Go server and not on the other invert the list with no front involved.

api_v1 GET /api/v1/admin/stats/timeserie.why: The bucket of a server's first dashboard sample after a reset, which it writes as it boots. The chain:admin cases read the same value in the same stage, and the M5 mutation control none (Go vs Go) showed both with 12:35:00 against 12:36:00, next to #admin.

api_v1 POST /api/v1/collections/#flow:co.why: A shared collection's v1 allowed_profile_ids lists every profile on the login sorted by ID (`v1CollectionAudience`, `slices.Sort`). Profiles created earlier in the plan get random UUIDs on each stack, so where they sort against the fixed seed IDs differs. Seen Go vs Go: `self-compare.sh --only 'flow:collections|flow:settings|scenario:profiles_create'` differed on these three cases at $.allowed_profile_ids[0..3] in 5 of 6 runs; the M6 proxy-all run showed create_second and parent_create at [1] and [2].

api_v2 GET /api/v2/playback/capabilities.why: These are the viewer's first capability read after a stage's restart. sourceBitratePercentile answers one with no bandwidth_probe_target_kbps and starts the read in the background, so the ETag changes once that read lands, and the replay gets 304 or 200 depending on which came first. Seen Go vs Go in both directions: the peer case in a lab run, and #user as 200 against 304 in 1 of 10 resets of both Go stacks.
